To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

10 biomarkers from distinct pathways predict the risk of cardiovascular disease and death, that a multimarker score based on the biomarkers is a strong predictor of cardiovascular risk, but that adding the multimarker score to conventional risk factors adds little to risk classification.
multiple biomarkers from diverse pathways add only slightly to conventional risk factors for predicting first major cardiovascular events and death.
the 10 contemporary risk markers that we studied add only moderately to standard clinical risk factors for predicting the risks of first major cardiovascular events and death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel biomarkers and their use in risk stratification.
the development of new biomarkers and the use of biomarkers to improve risk prediction.
the development of a new approach to the analysis of the risk of cardiovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for assessing risk in individual patients, the use of these 10 contemporary biomarker levels adds only moderately to the standard risk factors.

the use of multiple biomarkers adds only moderately to the prediction of cardiovascular risk, and the use of multiple markers is unlikely to have a substantial impact on the prevention of cardiovascular disease.
the use of the biomarker panel studied in this report adds little to the prediction of first major cardiovascular events or death, beyond the prediction afforded by conventional risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for the prediction of cardiovascular risk in individuals, the use of contemporary biomarkers adds only modestly to standard risk factors.
multiple contemporary biomarkers are useful, but the incremental benefit of adding them to conventional risk factors is small.
the use of multiple biomarkers in clinical practice is unlikely to improve risk stratification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a panel of biomarkers may provide a more comprehensive assessment of cardiovascular risk than any single biomarker.
the combination of these biomarkers is not a panacea.
a panel of multiple biomarkers can be used to predict the future occurrence of major cardiovascular events. (ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00005487.)
